name: Helium
tagline: Levyx's proprietary flash-optimised embeddable key-value engine (c. 2016–2019); company defunct.
description: Helium was a proprietary key-value storage engine from Levyx Inc. of Irvine, California, designed to index billions of objects per node on flash by bypassing much of the kernel I/O path and using Levyx's own data structures. It shipped as a library with C, C++, Java, Node.js and REST interfaces, offered range queries, search and transactions, and included compatibility wrappers for the Memcached, LevelDB and RocksDB APIs so it could be dropped under existing systems such as Spark shuffle, Kafka or caching layers. Levyx built its Xenon analytics platform and the Radon distributed object store on top of it. The company stopped operating around 2019 and the product is no longer available.
statusNote: Levyx ceased operations around 2019 and levyx.com no longer resolves; Helium is not available. Use RocksDB or Speedb instead.

pricing.notes: Historically licensed commercially; no longer sold.

scale.notes: Single-node engine aimed at billions of objects on flash; scale-out came from Levyx's Xenon and Radon layers.

strengths: Flash-first design with kernel-bypass I/O paths
Drop-in wrappers for Memcached, LevelDB and RocksDB APIs
Range queries and transactions in an embeddable library
weaknesses: Vendor is gone; no binaries, support or source
Closed source, so performance claims were never independently reproducible
useCases: Historical reference for flash-optimised key-value engines
Context when evaluating API-compatible RocksDB or Memcached replacements
